clue.text: Deity leads a double life

indicators.note: a double of something is two copies, so the short word is written out twice

parts.note: life is being, and 'is' expresses existence, as in 'I think, therefore I am'

explanation.surface: A god lives a secret second existence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' asks for IS twice. The surface also hints that Isis, as Oxford's name for the Thames, is a river with a second identity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian goddess of magic and motherhood, wife of Osiris, is a classic example of a deity.

clue.text: Time inside too cold at first — being kept under wraps

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word cold is wanted here
the time abbreviation goes within the word for excessively

parts.note: too, as in too much, means excessively

explanation.surface: Something cold is being stored under covers for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something secretly or in hiding is doing it under wraps, an idiom for concealment.

clue.text: Male attached to one palindromic female …

definitions.text: Male attached to one palindromic female

indicators.note: the male abbreviation is joined on after the woman's name

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name that reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: A man is bound to a woman whose name reads the same either way.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the first man of Genesis, joined to Eve, herself a palindrome; the trailing dots lead into the next clue's 'another'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first man is partnered with Eve, whose three-letter name reads identically backwards.

clue.text: … and another holding ring, small expression of adoration

indicators.note: the woman's name contains the ring and the small abbreviation

parts.note: carrying on from the previous clue, another palindromic woman's name is Hannah
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A second woman wears a little ring as a token of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' depends on the previous clue: a second woman's name that reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This variant spelling of the cry used in Christian worship is a shout of praise to God.

clue.text: Creator of printed works, 100 in number

indicators.note: the Roman hundred goes inside the anaesthetic

parts.note: read as numb-er, something that numbs: the old anaesthetic ether
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A prolific author has produced a hundred books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but 'numb-er', a thing that numbs.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist who bites designs into metal plates with acid produces prints from them.

clue.text: One foreign coin produced after complaint about new kind

indicators.note: the number and coin come after the complaint
the complaint word goes round the new abbreviation

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cent is a coin in the US and euro zone, foreign to British readers

explanation.surface: A single overseas coin is handed over after a grumble about a new variety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kind' looks like a noun meaning type, but it is the adjective generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beneficent does good to others, which is being generous and benevolent.

clue.text: Demanding part, central character in Othello

parts.note: to part is to sever or cut apart

indicators.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter play title is wanted

explanation.surface: A tough role: the lead character in Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central character' sounds like the title role, but it is only the fourth of seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe test or regime is a demanding, rigorous one.

clue.text: Finishes off prize crossword, being very nervous

indicators.note: the final letter of each of the next four words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone completes the prize puzzle and is very anxious about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very' is not an intensifier on the definition; it gives its last letter like the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling on edge, tense and jumpy is being nervous.

clue.text: Potential share for peacemaker — that's how this ends

definitions.text: Potential share for peacemaker — that's how this ends

parts.words: Potential share for peacemaker — that's how this ends
parts.note: Isaiah says weapons will be beaten into ploughshares; the blade a peacemaker would turn into a share is the weapon, and the answer ends up as one

explanation.surface: A cryptic hint at the biblical promise of weapons turned into farming tools.
explanation.walkthrough: A share here is a ploughshare, the cutting blade of a plough, not a portion. Isaiah's 'swords into ploughshares' gives the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical prophecy says blades of war will be hammered into plough blades, so this weapon is a share in waiting.

clue.text: Getting better, those people conclude, after operating

indicators.note: the pronoun and the verb come after the operating word

parts.note: a machine that is operating is on
them refers to those people
to conclude is to end

explanation.surface: A surgeon's patients recover, and the operation closes.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for recovering from illness or improving after a setback.

clue.text: Play cricket on second XI, followed by hot relaxing treatment

indicators.note: the batting word follows the side
the hot abbreviation comes last

parts.note: a cricket or football XI is a team of eleven
to bat is to play cricket, taking a turn with the bat
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: The reserve eleven play cricket and then enjoy a hot spa session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second XI' looks like the B team, but S and TEAM are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting in a room full of hot vapour is a soothing spa treatment.

clue.text: Abrasive European happy taking one right away

indicators.note: taking with away tells us a letter is removed from the happy word
away completes taking away, which removes the right abbreviation

parts.note: merry means happy and cheerful
a single R, the abbreviation for right; the happy word has two

explanation.surface: A cheerful European drives off with a correct answer.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Rs in MERRY is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark granular rock is ground for sandpaper and nail files, so it is an abrasive.

clue.text: From vessel I'm able to see inside Rome

parts.note: a vat is a large vessel for liquids
I'm able means I can

explanation.surface: From a tub, a person claims to be able to view inside Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is the noun, a bishop's seat, as in the Holy See, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal city-state is the Holy See, the seat of the Pope enclosed within the city of Rome.

clue.text: Temperature in medicine bottle's key

indicators.note: the temperature letter is placed within the small bottle

parts.note: a vial is a small bottle for medicine

explanation.surface: A medicine bottle's essential reading is the temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Something key is essential or crucial, which is what vital means.

clue.text: Eye trousers initially exchanged — they're said to be trendy

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words trade places

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
cords are corduroy trousers

explanation.surface: An eye catches some trousers swapped round, supposedly fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap W and C at the starts of WATCH CORDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular slogans or buzzwords are fashionable expressions repeated by everyone.

clue.text: Object when put in torn garments

indicators.note: the purpose word is placed inside the torn word

parts.note: rent is the past tense of rend, so torn
an object is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A thing is placed among ripped clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' is a noun meaning goal, not the verb to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic or literary word means clothing.

clue.text: It's in the tax once faithfully paid

indicators.note: the pronoun is set inside the definite article

parts.note: the 's stands for is, so the pronoun is what goes in

explanation.surface: It's included in the levy that people once paid dutifully.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of produce or income was given to the church, a levy paid by the faithful.

clue.text: Stormy, is it? After regular cancellations, agree to meet

indicators.note: every other letter of the phrase is struck out, leaving the alternate letters

explanation.surface: Is the weather stormy? Once the regular cancellations end, we agree to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike S, O, M, I, I from STORMYISIT.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, this means to arrange a romantic rendezvous, usually secret, with a lover.

clue.text: Feature of dress that may attract attention

definitions.meaning: the folded and sewn edge of a skirt or dress
a little cough or throat-clearing sound, as in ahem, used to get someone's notice

explanation.surface: A dress detail that might catch the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the turned-up edge of cloth, and the throat-clearing noise made to be noticed.

clue.text: Wartime emergency gear for pilots in a mess, wet after coming to grief

indicators.note: letters that have come to grief are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Pilots' survival kit lies in a soggy heap after a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange A MESS WET.
explanation.definitionFit: RAF airmen named their inflatable life jackets after the buxom Hollywood star.

clue.text: Promote officer after fire returned

indicators.note: the officer comes after the turned word
the word for dismissing is read backwards

parts.note: to fire someone is to axe them
LT is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An officer is promoted after a sacking is reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AXE into EXA.
explanation.definitionFit: To exalt someone is to raise them to a higher rank or praise them highly.

clue.text: For instance, they include ant since also an insect

definitions.text: For instance, they include ant since also an insect

parts.words: For instance, they include ant since also an insect
parts.note: the letters of ant since rearrange to instance, and since becomes insect, so the clue is full of examples of letter rearrangements

explanation.surface: A nature-lover's claim that one creature counts as another.
explanation.walkthrough: ANT SINCE rearranges to INSTANCE, and SINCE to INSECT, so the clue demonstrates what it defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Words made by rearranging another word's letters, as in the clue's own examples.

clue.text: Crass advice about people's survival 'sans pain'?

definitions.text: Crass advice about people's survival 'sans pain'?

parts.words: Crass advice about people's survival 'sans pain'?
parts.note: sans pain is French for without bread; the remark attributed to Marie Antoinette told the starving to have pastry instead

explanation.surface: A heartless suggestion about how people might survive painlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pain' is French for bread, not suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: The callous retort supposedly made by Marie Antoinette to news that peasants had no bread.

clue.text: Nice view? Some parts are like that

definitions.meaning: from Nice, the French Riviera city, you look out on the Mediterranean, the Med
parties or puzzles built round a subject are described as having a theme

explanation.surface: A pleasant outlook, and some areas are similar.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, so its view is THE MED.
explanation.definitionFit: Read whole, the word describes things organised round a particular subject, like parts of this puzzle.

clue.text: One sailor, saying nothing, turned up in Asian port

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
AB is an able-bodied seaman
keeping mum means staying silent

explanation.surface: A tight-lipped sailor appeared in a port in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Read I AB MUM from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: The major Indian city on the Arabian Sea, formerly Bombay, is a great seaport.

clue.text: See 22
Cardinal, say, disrupting firm belief

indicators.note: the colour breaks into the company abbreviation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
cardinal is a shade of red, so red is an example

explanation.surface: A churchman upsets a strongly held conviction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' is the colour, not the cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin word for 'I believe' names a statement of faith or principles.

clue.text: Make sound of one bird or another

definitions.meaning: a cockerel's cry, to make a cock's call
a second bird, the large black corvid

explanation.surface: Imitate a bird call, or a different bird's.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the cockerel's call and the black corvid bird.

clue.text: He reported storm at sea, danger to shipping

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so we use how the word is heard

parts.note: he refers to a man, a male

indicators.note: confused and adrift, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man told of a tempest out on the ocean that menaced boats.
explanation.walkthrough: Say MALE to get MAEL, then rearrange STORM into STROM.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful whirlpool in the sea, which can drag down vessels.

clue.text: Part of West End not quite as fashionable

parts.note: so can mean as, in 'not so big' = 'not as big'

indicators.note: the phrase falls just short, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: hot means trendy and fashionable

explanation.surface: A district of London's West End is not quite as trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: SOHO is a district of London's West End, known for nightlife and restaurants.
explanation.definitionFit: This London district lies in the city's West End entertainment area.

clue.text: Before university, people posted list of courses

indicators.note: the people come before the university letter

parts.note: men, as soldiers posted to a station

explanation.surface: Before going to college, students got a list of classes in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests academic study, but the list is a restaurant's dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's bill of fare sets out the dishes, its courses.

clue.text: Make too many plans? Not a good balance

definitions.meaning: a negative bank balance, with more taken out than put in

explanation.surface: Over-planning is not a healthy equilibrium.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank account overdrawn below zero has a debit, a poor balance; and to over-draft is to plan too much.

clue.text: Chaps who work out rapprochement, in part

indicators.note: only a stretch of the long word is used, taking its letters from within

explanation.surface: Men who negotiate a reconciliation, partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work out' looks like settle the rapprochement, but it means exercise in the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscular, macho men are the sort found exercising in gyms.
